summary.whatChanges: Content negotiation now honors quality value 0 as an explicit rejection. The `accepts` helper filters out `q=0` entries before matching, and the header-based language detector skips languages with `q=0`. Tests cover both, including wildcard rejection and falling through to the next detector.
behaviorChanges: An Accept header entry with q=0 (e.g. `application/json;q=0`) no longer matches a supported type; the configured default is returned instead
A wildcard rejected with q=0 (e.g. `application/*;q=0`) no longer matches types in that range
Accept-Language entries with q=0 are no longer detected; detection falls through to remaining entries, the next detector, or the fallback language
Requests like `/?lang=ja` with `accept-language: fr;q=0` now resolve via the querystring detector and set the language cookie accordingly
risks: Applications that previously relied on q=0 entries still matching will now receive the default/fallback value, changing served content type or language
The accepts helper may now return the configured default more often when clients send q=0 entries, even if other acceptable types exist that were previously reachable
